correctness.rationale: Every equation is an integral linear word and gives a homomorphism \(G^k\to dG\), with \(d=\gcd(m,c_1,\ldots,c_k)\), by Bézout. The equation \(dx=0\) realizes every \(d\mid m\); its multiplication-only equivalent is \(x^{m+d}=x^m\). Uniform fibers give \(|G[d]|/|G|\). Primary cyclic decomposition yields \(f_p(j)=\sum_i\min(j,\lambda_i)\), whose successive differences count blocks of length at least \(j\). Positive weakly decreasing increments reconstruct the elementary-divisor multiset. Endpoint, integrality, and independent Cartesian-product conditions prove necessity and inverse sufficiency; the case \(N=1\) is separate. Direct arithmetic verifies all 516 groups of order at most 256 and 604 two-variable equations; finite testing is corroboration, not general proof.

originality.rationale: The two original 2026 papers were read at the definition, direct-product propositions, cyclic prime-power lemma, minimal-spectrum theorem and adjoining proofs. Those assertions treat smaller classes or give only product inclusions, and they do not imply the general synchronized p-primary profile equality, inverse realizability conditions and isomorphism reconstruction without additional new arguments. Targeted published-record searches revealed no direct result. Classical classification makes a related older formulation possible; this is noted as residual risk rather than disproved.
residual_risks: An older isomorphism-recovery theorem for distributions of element orders or power-map kernel cardinalities may be convertible to the inverse step even if its title does not mention probabilistic equations. This possibility was not exhaustively excluded.

The structural finite-abelian classification and torsion counting are classical inputs; originality attaches to their combined exact equational-spectrum inverse formulation rather than to elementary-divisor theory itself.

value.rationale: Cardó’s 2026 program poses equational probability spectra as algebraic invariants and classifies their minimal case. The final theorem solves the natural exact forward-and-inverse problem for the complete class of finite abelian groups, including which rational sets are possible, a unique reconstruction algorithm from UNLABELLED probabilities, and the nontrivial distinction between equal-exponent cardinality and genuine isomorphism rigidity. Mixed-exponent factors show direct-product spectrum inclusion cannot be treated as equality, and inverse prime-concavity/product conditions are needed; this is a complete natural classification, not arbitrary finite table recomputation or routine substitution.
